rounds.text: MPS Ltd trades at a moderate P/E of 20.6x [E1] while delivering extraordinary capital efficiency, highlighted by an ROE of 29.7% [E13] and an elite ROCE of 38.7% [E12]. This fundamental quality is further underscored by a stellar DCF intrinsic valuation of Rs 4401 per share, offering a substantial 48.0% margin of safety against the current market price of Rs 2287 [E45, E46]. Growth momentum remains firmly intact across key divisions, evidenced by Education Q4 revenue surging 30.5% year-over-year [E77] and total quarterly revenue jumping 20.4% to INR 224.24 crores [E79]. Operational execution is exceptional, driving EBITDA up 53.0% with margins expanding to 34.3% [E80], while management confidently reiterates guidance to comfortably cross INR 300 crores in EBITDA by FY27 [E87]. Furthermore, balance sheet health is pristine with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x [E37] and robust free cash flow reaching Rs 188 Cr in March 2026 [E36]. Conceded: the dividend yield sits at 0.00% [E4], and the P/B of 5.56x trades at a premium to the broader sector benchmark of 1.08x [E7].

MPS Ltd currently trades at a significant premium to its sector, with a P/E of 21.12x compared to the 16x benchmark and a P/B of 5.56x against a sector benchmark of just 1.08x [E6, E7]. This valuation disconnect is further highlighted by an EV/EBITDA of 13.55x, which sits well above the sector's 8.96x [E11]. Despite the company's growth narrative, investors face a total lack of income, as the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. The stock also carries substantial historical risk, evidenced by a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.1% [E53]. Furthermore, foreign institutional interest has waned, with holdings dropping from 3.71% in December 2023 to 1.49% in September 2026 [E42]. Conceded: the company maintains strong profitability metrics, including a 29.7% ROE and a 38.7% ROCE [E12, E13].

The bear’s focus on valuation multiples ignores the fundamental reality that MPS Ltd is a high-quality compounder, not a generic sector peer. While the P/E and P/B ratios appear elevated [E6, E7], they are justified by an ROE of 29.7% and an ROCE of 38.7%, which dwarf the sector benchmarks of 4.31% and 5.42% respectively [E9, E10, E13]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. The EV/EBITDA premium [E11] is a reflection of the company’s aggressive growth, evidenced by a 23% compounded profit growth over five years and a 16% increase in the trailing twelve months [E19, E21]. Regarding the historical drawdown [E53], it is irrelevant to the current financial health of a company that is now almost debt-free [E59] and maintains a robust cash conversion ratio of 1.14x [E34]. Finally, the decline in foreign institutional holdings [E42] is countered by the fact that domestic institutions have increased their stake [E43], resulting in an overall positive institutional money flow [E44].

The bull’s reliance on high ROE and ROCE [E9, E10, E13] ignores that these metrics are currently decoupled from share price performance, which has seen 0% growth over the last year [E25]. While the bull cites aggressive profit growth [E19, E21], it fails to address that the company’s operating-margin trend is inconsistent [E32, E33], casting doubt on the sustainability of these margins. Conceded: the company is almost debt-free [E59]. However, the bull’s dismissal of valuation multiples [E6, E7, E11] as mere reflections of quality is dangerous when the stock trades at a significant premium to sector benchmarks, including a P/B ratio of 5.56x against a 1.08x sector average [E7]. Furthermore, the bull’s claim of positive institutional sentiment [E44] is undermined by the material exit of foreign institutions, whose holdings dropped from 3.71% to 1.49% [E42]. Finally, the bull ignores that the company’s earnings growth is decelerating [E67] and that net profit has shown a 5% year-over-year decline in some metrics [E66], suggesting that the market is rightfully skeptical of the company's ability to maintain its historical growth trajectory.
